papers.title: RobPiCFM: A Training-Free Target-Conditioned Method with Foundation Models for Robotic Picking in Clutter
papers.summary: Picking objects from clutter remains a challenging problem in robotic manipulation, as it requires connecting object-level perception, grasp generation, collision-aware selection, and robot motion execution in unstructured scenes. In this paper, we present RobPiCFM, an open-source, trainingfree method for target-conditioned picking in cluttered scenes. The proposed method combines pretrained foundation-modelbased perception with RGB-D geometry, 6D object pose estimation and tracking, grasp candidate generation, constraintbased grasp filtering, and motion planning. papers.title: Time-Inhomogeneity in Risk Averse Objectives for Financial Applications of Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: In finance, sequential decision problems are often faced, for which reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a promising tool for optimisation without the need of analytical tractability. However, the objective of classical RL is the expected cumulated reward, while financial applications typically require a trade-off between return and risk. In this work, we focus on settings where one cares about the time split of the total return, ruling out most risk-aware generalisations of RL which optimise a risk measure defined on the latter. papers.title: Making Tail Constraints Bind: Two Silent Failure Modes in CVaR-Constrained Portfolio RL
papers.summary: A portfolio allocator trained by reinforcement learning (RL) to maximise return has no reason to avoid large losses. The usual safeguard caps Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), the average loss in the worst weeks, through a Lagrangian penalty. We show that this safeguard can fail silently in two ways. First, when the penalty and the reward sit on different scales, through an unstandardised cost advantage or a dual step mis-scaled to the CVaR excess, the penalty weight stays at zero and the budget is never enforced, even as tail metrics keep improving. papers.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
papers.summary: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. papers.title: Autonomous navigation of multiple reconfigurable ferrofluid droplet robots in complex environments
papers.summary: Ferrofluid-based soft robots with extreme deformability have emerged as promising manipulation tools for diverse biomedical applications. Their unique properties to navigate irregular terrains and access otherwise unreachable regions within confined spaces have enabled new opportunities in targeted drug delivery, microfluidic logistics, and lab/organ on-a-chip. However, achieving dynamic motion planning and intelligent behavior for multiple reconfigurable ferrofluid droplet robots (FDRs) is still one of the major challenges yet to be solved. papers.title: Primitives and Paths: Predicting What Post-Training Can Do from What the Base Model Already Has
papers.summary: Does reinforcement learning teach language models new capabilities, or merely amplify ones acquired during pre-training? The literature offers evidence for both: pass@$k$ studies suggest RL reweights latent behaviours while some controlled composition studies demonstrate gains beyond simple amplification. We argue that this question has no answer independent of the capability state of the base model, and propose a two-dimensional state space for post-trainability. papers.title: Reinforcement learning as a comparative framework for the science of agency
papers.summary: Agency is attributed to a wide range of organisms across the tree of life. However, there is currently no systematic approach by which to investigate and compare agential phenomena and the diversity of agenthood. In this paper, I explore reinforcement learning (RL) as a candidate comparative framework for the science of agency. In Section 2, I introduce the history of RL and trace its roots in experimental research on animal learning before turning to its integration with computational methods and usage across disciplines. papers.title: MQViT-OSR: geometric-aware vision transformer for omnidirectional super resolution with multiquadric interpolation
papers.summary: Omnidirectional images (ODIs) are capable of showing the entire 360° of real-world scenes used in immersive fields of surveillance, robotics, and virtual reality. Most ODIs are obtained at low resolutions, which cause blurred edges, geometric distortions. To handle these problems, MQViT-OSR is proposed that captures long-range spatial dependencies and efficiently reconstructs panoramic images with a high level of fidelity and resolution. papers.title: Dream-Butterfly: Configuring Embodied Conversational Guidance for Public Outdoor Mixed Reality Exhibitions
papers.summary: Public outdoor mixed reality (MR) exhibitions make guidance a spatial interaction problem: visitors need timely explanations while roaming open sites, attending to virtual artworks, hazards, bystanders, and route choices. We present Dream-Butterfly, a field-deployed embodied conversational guide for campus-scale outdoor MR exhibitions. First, the planar motion of a ground robot and the vertical orientation of the target are exploited to derive a constrained plane-induced homography with four effective degrees of freedom. papers.title: Comb Machine: Mediated Intimacy in Telerobotics
papers.summary: Comb Machine: Almost Intimate (2025) is a teleoperated robotic installation in which a human comber remotely combs participants’ hair through a robot arm. Through delayed disclosure, participants first encounter the robot as seemingly autonomous and later discover the human labor behind the gesture. This mechanism changes the perceived agency and meaning of the experienced touch while heightening attention to hidden human labor behind automation. papers.title: ‘Photoshopping’ Robotic Movement for Human-Machine Creativity
papers.summary: This paper explores manipulating images through robotic motion rather than pixels. We used a motion capture system to record the trajectory of a calligraphy brush as an artist painted the classical Chinese orchid subject matter. We used this recording to recreate the painting with a robotic arm fitted with the same brush, then parametrically transformed the data to create new variations and experiments. This paper explores the creative agency of the artist, the motion editor, the robot and the physical materials, and how we might think of robotics as a domain for digital image editing.

papers.title: Reflecting on Future Human-AI Society through Along the River During the Qingming Festival
papers.summary: How can a historical city image help us reflect on possible futures of human-AI society? This project proposes a creative process that uses historical imagery as a starting point for translating interpretations of past social life into AI-related visual refigurations. Based on this process, we developed an AI-assisted interactive system using Along the River During the Qingming Festival. The system guides users from observing details in the scroll to constructing AI-related visual speculations. papers.summary: L'Italia dispone di una base manifatturiera tra le più automatizzate d'Europa, ma continua a registrare una crescita debole della produttività. papers.title: Mixed Reality Teleoperation with Object-Aware Digital Twins
papers.summary: Remote robot teleoperation often relies on direct visual access to the physical workspace, limiting collaboration in hazardous or restricted environments. While Mixed Reality (MR) interfaces and Digital Twins (DTs) improve robot visualization, manipulable objects are rarely synchronized, preventing fully remote interaction. FlexMARL: Graph-Driven Rollout-Training Co-Design for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Despite algorithm-level innovations for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the underlying infrastructure for large-scale MARL remains underexplored. Existing training frameworks primarily optimize for single-agent scenarios and fail to capture the graph-structured nature of MARL. This fundamental mismatch leads to three MARL-specific challenges: topology-induced rollout skew, critical path synchronization barriers, and dynamic training demand.
